piezas.titulo: El malestar psicológico a través del inglés y otros idiomas
piezas.resumenOriginal: El malestar psicológico a través del inglés y otros idiomas emcamara 29/10/2026 26/11/2026 Fecha y hora: 26/11/26, 5pm CET Ponentes : Anna-Maria Bucur, Dalle Molle Institute for Artificial Intelligence, Università della Svizzera italiana (Italia) Presentador: Paolo Rosso, Universidad Politécnica de Valencia (España). Resumen: La presentación analiza cómo el procesamiento del lenguaje natural puede respaldar la investigación psicológica analizando interacciones procedentes de redes sociales para comprender mejor el malestar psicológico. Mientras que el PLN resulta eficaz a la hora de identificar patrones lingüísticos, la psicología articula la investigación definiendo los conceptos clave, explicando su relevancia y aportando un marco para interpretar los hallazgos. La ponencia comienza con varios estudios de caso centrados en la supervivencia al cáncer, la identificación de problemas de salud mental en la población general y la exploración de momentos de felicidad en personas diagnosticadas con depresión, todos ellos a partir de datos en inglés. A continuación, aborda consideraciones transculturales al trabajar con datos en idiomas distintos del inglés y evalúa los modelos del lenguaje de gran tamaño (LLM) para este fin. La presentación subraya que un PLN fundamentado en la teoría puede desvelar trayectorias psicológicas y ofrecer perspectivas valiosas para las intervenciones terapéuticas. No obstante, también destaca cómo la falta de datos de calidad y de evaluaciones adecuadas plantea retos a la hora de desarrollar métodos aplicables a lenguas más allá del inglés. Reseña: Ana-Maria Bucur es investigadora postdoctoral en el Instituto Dalle Molle de Inteligencia Artificial (IDSIA), Università della Svizzera italiana, donde trabaja en el Laboratorio de Recuperación de Información del profesor Fabio Crestani. Realizó un doctorado en cotutela entre la Universitat Politècnica de València y la Universidad de Bucarest, bajo la dirección de los profesores Paolo Rosso y Liviu P. Dinu. Ana-Maria ha participado en colaboraciones interdisciplinares que abarcan tanto la psicología como las humanidades digitales. Su investigación se centra principalmente en el procesamiento del lenguaje natural (PLN) aplicado a la salud mental, investigando en especial cómo las personas expresan sus estados psicológicos a través del lenguaje y de qué manera los métodos computacionales pueden mejorar nuestra comprensión de la salud mental y respaldar el bienestar. Más recientemente, ha estado explorando cómo influye la cultura en las manifestaciones de los trastornos mentales y cómo desarrollar métodos computacionales con sensibilidad cultural para un cribado de salud mental más inclusivo. Enlace a la charla : https://zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_i2j1MGK0TCStUlwD-gevgQ

piezas.titulo: Multimodal profiling and intersectional genetics reveal CA1 border inhibitory neuron diversity and postnatal emergence of retrosplenial connectivity
piezas.resumenOriginal: Inhibitory neurons (INs) at the stratum radiatum/stratum lacunosum-moleculare border of hippocampal CA1 comprise diverse populations, including long-range-projecting neurons that innervate the retrosplenial cortex (RSCtx). However, their molecular organization and developmental connectivity remain poorly understood. Here, we combine multimodal transcriptomic profiling, intersectional genetics, and retrograde tracing to characterize CA1 border INs. We identified two major caudal ganglionic eminence-derived, Cxcl14-enriched populations distinguished by Syt6/Cck-related and Ntng1-expressing transcriptional profiles. We then generated a Cxcl14-Cre mouse line that, when combined with an IN-specific viral enhancer, provides genetic access to CA1 border INs. Retrograde labeling established that CA1 INs projecting to the RSCtx belong to the Ntng1-expressing population, and that this long-range projection emerges during postnatal mouse development, between postnatal days 3 and 5. Finally, analysis of genes encoding cell-surface proteins, key regulators of connectivity, revealed distinct expression profiles in RSCtx-projecting and SYT6-positive INs. Together, these findings establish a molecular and developmental framework for CA1 border IN diversity and provide a genetic strategy for investigating the assembly and function of these inhibitory circuits.

Esta evidencia abre la puerta a manipular genéticamente esas vías para explorar su papel en la memoria espacial.

piezas.resumenOriginal: Aims To explore the feasibility, satisfaction with, enjoyment of, acceptability, and preliminary effects of joint virtual reality (VR) sessions targeting physical engagement in youth with disabilities and relaxation in caregivers. Methods In a mini-ethnographic case study, four youth-caregiver dyads completed weekly 30-minute immersive VR sessions over four weeks. Youth (aged 10-20 years) with cerebral palsy ( n = 2), autism with motor dyspraxia ( n = 1), and CHARGE syndrome ( n = 1) used the AstroSurfer app targeting motor functions. Caregivers simultaneously engaged with the TRIPP ® app for relaxation and meditation. Pre- and post-intervention measures included the Trunk Control Measurement Scale and the Quality of Upper Extremity Skills Test (youth), the Parental Stress Scale and the Depression, Anxiety and Stress Scale (caregivers). Enjoyment ratings (0-10, at each session) and exit interviews were completed. Results Although standardized motor outcomes showed limited overall change over the intervention period, improvements were observed in one youth participant. Reductions in stress were noted for three caregivers. Enjoyment ratings were high (7-10/10 for youth; 9-10/10 for caregivers), with engaging gameplay and relaxation identified as key benefits. Conclusions Findings provide preliminary support for the potential feasibility and acceptability of family-centered VR interventions in pediatric rehabilitation, warranting evaluation in larger studies.

piezas.titulo: Peer Mentoring Benefits in Rehabilitation for Individuals With Spinal Cord Injury: A Systematic Review.
piezas.resumenOriginal: Importance The lived experiences of peer mentors with spinal cord injury (SCI) provide distinct value in the rehabilitation process and contribute to improved outcomes. When combined with traditional therapy, peer mentorship programs can enhance life satisfaction among individuals living with SCI. Objective To explore the impact that peer-led mentorship programs and interventions have on the rehabilitation outcomes for individuals with a spinal cord injury (SCI). Data sources PubMed, MEDLINE, PsycINFO, CINAHL, ERIC, Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, MedNar, and OpenGrey were searched between 2014 and 2024. The Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool was adapted and used to assess risk of bias in the included studies. Study selection and data collection Inclusion criteria included individuals with SCI who participated in peer mentorship and reported outcomes on quality of life, well-being, independence, or activities of daily living (ADLs) or instrumental ADLs. Exclusion criteria included interventions conducted via telehealth or reported outcomes of social participation. Findings Five articles were analyzed for synthesis, which included individuals 18 yr and older with an SCI. Findings support peer mentorship as an important component of rehabilitation. Findings may have limited generalizability across different settings and populations because of the small number of available studies and variability in study designs, interventions, and outcome measures. None of the articles reviewed included occupational therapists. Conclusions and relevance This review highlighted the benefits of peer mentorship in enhanced life satisfaction. Findings support peer mentorship as an important component of rehabilitation. Future research should examine the benefits of incorporating peer-led intervention programs across the continuum of care, including occupational therapy, in enhancing best practices in SCI rehabilitation. Plain-Language Summary: Peer mentorship programs can help people with spinal cord injuries adjust to daily life by providing guidance, support, and encouragement that professionals without lived experience may not offer. This review found that peer mentoring can improve psychological well-being and health management and reduce unplanned hospital visits. Evidence is limited because of the small number of studies and variations in study design; however, the results suggest that meaningful benefits may be present. Further research is needed to determine the most effective way to implement peer mentorship across rehabilitation settings.

piezas.titulo: Two Nonprofits Join Forces to Support Adolescents on Autism Spectrum
piezas.resumenOriginal: Two Nonprofits Join Forces to Support Adolescents on Autism Spectrum STAR Admin Thu, 06/15/2017 - 14:07 STAR Institute for Sensory Processing Disorder (SPD) and T.A.C.T. (Teaching the Autism Community Trades) are two Colorado nonprofits who have partnered to create a series of respite camps serving adolescents who have autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Developmental Pathways has awarded the organizations a $25,000 grant to fund three F.U.S.E. (Fostering Unlimited Success and Empowerment) camps through 2018. STAR Institute offers premier treatment for SPD and brings expertise in social skills while T.AC.T. teaches trade and life skills to individuals with ASD and SPD with an emphasis on fostering independence and personal growth. “This is a very rare and exciting way to see two nonprofits interact. Our partnership to create F.U.S.E. allows both of our organizations to combine expertise in a way that best serves these adolescents to find new interests and gain the soft skills to successfully participate in peer groups and future workplaces”, says Dick Layton, Director of STAR Institute for SPD. The respite camps will be week-long day camps that host six students per camp ages 12-15 who have autism spectrum disorder. The camps will teach pre-vocational and vocational skills in a supportive, social, and inclusionary environment. Each camp has a different project for participants including: building a non-motorized go-cart with a partner, building an instrument to play in a band, and crafting board games. “The intended focus of F.U.S.E. is not just about offering a respite program for families. By generating new experiences for these adolescents, we hope to foster new skills, new interests, develop social skills, and give them a sense of empowerment to participate in what hopefully becomes a new hobby or future career interest”, says Danny Combs co-founder and president of T.A.C.T. SPD is a neurological disorder that disrupts the way an individual processes and responds to sensations. The disorder can affect people in only one sense–for example, just touch or just sight or just movement–or in multiple senses. One person with SPD may over-respond to touch sensation and find clothing, physical contact, other tactile sensory input to be unbearable and/or they may respond to visual or auditory or another sensory input. Another person might under-respond and show little or no reaction to stimulation, even pain or extreme hot and cold or just may be slow to respond to sensation. SPD and ASD have a high co-morbidity rate, but are also found to be standalone disorders. ASD refers to conditions categorized by challenges with social skills, repetitive behaviors, speech and nonverbal communication, as well as by unique strengths and differences that can occur on a range from mild to severe. Individuals with ASD and SPD frequently struggle with interpersonal skills over their lifetime and are often underestimated, which can lead to specific difficulty in career and relationships. F.U.S.E. aims to give individuals the ability to ignite new interests and feel empowered in group collaboration, which can lead to greater success in career and relationships. About STAR Institute for Sensory Processing Disorder: The STAR Institute for Sensory Processing Disorder, a Colorado 501(c)(3), is the world leader in treatment, research, and education for Sensory Processing Disorder, a neurological condition that disrupts the daily lives of more than 4 million Americans. The STAR Institute is the premier treatment center for children, adults and families living with Sensory Processing Disorder, feeding disorders, and other sensory conditions associated with ADHD, autism, and other developmental disorders. piezas.titulo: Occupational therapy interventions for functional neurological disorder: a scoping review
piezas.resumenOriginal: IntroductionFunctional Neurological Disorder (FND) is a common and disabling condition for which multidisciplinary rehabilitation is recommended; however, the specific contribution of occupational therapy remains poorly defined. This scoping review aimed to map and characterize occupational therapy interventions for people with FND, examine how these are delivered and evaluated within rehabilitation and identify priorities for future research.MethodsA scoping review was conducted using Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology. Peer-reviewed English-language intervention studies involving adults (≥18 years) with FND who received occupational therapy delivered independently or as part of multidisciplinary rehabilitation and reporting treatment outcomes were included. Descriptive analysis was undertaken. OVID Medline, Embase, APA PsycInfo and CINAHL Plus were searched from inception to July 2026, supplemented by reference list screening.ResultsForty-one studies (n= 1,284 participants; sample sizes 1–201) were included, with only one randomized study. Occupational therapy was predominantly delivered within multidisciplinary rehabilitation; only one study included a subgroup receiving occupational therapy alone. Despite considerable variation in intervention reporting, common occupational therapy intervention components included facilitating occupational engagement, movement retraining and anxiety management, with symptom management strategies integrated into functional activities to promote confidence and independence. Improvements in symptom severity, functional ability, mental health, and quality of life were reported following multidisciplinary rehabilitation including occupational therapy. However, findings were primarily derived from uncontrolled studies, and interpretation was further limited by heterogeneity in intervention approaches, inconsistent use of outcome measures, and variable follow-up.DiscussionAlthough occupational therapy was included in all eligible studies, occupational therapy-specific interventions and associated outcomes were inconsistently described and evaluated, limiting understanding of occupational therapy's distinct contribution within multidisciplinary rehabilitation. Future research should focus on clearly defining and evaluating the components of occupational therapy interventions.

piezas.titulo: Chronic unpredictable stress induces negative cognitive bias in rats with sex-specific changes in neurogenesis and functional connectivity
piezas.resumenOriginal: Background: Females are more likely to be diagnosed with major depressive disorder (MDD) than males. Cognitive symptoms of MDD include negative cognitive bias, the perception of ambiguous situations as negative, which predicts MDD episode onset and severity. MDD is associated with changes to functional connectivity between regions involved in cognition, emotion, attention, and memory. Methods: Here we examined the impact of chronic unpredictable stress (CUS) on negative cognitive bias in male (n=18) and female (n=22) Sprague-Dawley rats. We assessed hippocampal neurogenesis and c-Fos expression in response to an ambiguous context across 15 regions of the frontal cortex, amygdala, nucleus accumbens, and hippocampus, including in newborn dentate gyrus (DG) neurons, to examine functional connectivity during cognitive bias testing. We conducted a graph-based network analysis and constructed linear models to predict freezing in the ambiguous context based on regional activation. Results: CUS-exposed rats froze more to the ambiguous context than non-CUS-exposed rats, regardless of sex. CUS decreased neurogenesis in the ventral DG of both sexes, and increased activation of new neurons in the dorsal DG of males only. In response to the ambiguous context, CUS males had an increase in c-Fos expression in the amygdala. CUS produced extensive, sex-specific network reorganization, decreasing global network efficiency in males but not in females. Freezing in the ambiguous context was predicted by activation of new neurons in combination with the ventral CA1 in opposing directions across sex. Conclusions: These findings suggest that sex-specific pathways drive the expression of CUS-induced negative cognitive bias, underscoring the necessity of sex-stratified preclinical and clinical research on negative cognitive bias in depression.

piezas.titulo: Imaging findings and clinical outcomes in neonates with isolated subependymal echogenicity on cranial ultrasound: a retrospective cohort study
piezas.resumenOriginal: ObjectiveTo describe clinical and imaging findings in neonates with isolated subependymal echogenicity on cranial ultrasound and examine associations with recorded mortality and cerebral palsy.MethodsThis retrospective single-center cohort included 317 neonates admitted between January 2015 and December 2018 with an initial ultrasound finding suspicious for isolated subependymal hemorrhage. Clinical records, available MRI findings, and follow-up information were reviewed. Cerebral palsy was ascertained from rehabilitation or neurology diagnostic records, supplemented by telephone follow-up in January 2026, independently of developmental test scores. The primary adjusted analysis compared death with all survivors using an exploratory six-item comorbidity count and clinical covariates; hospitalization duration was excluded, and laterality was coded as unilateral or bilateral.ResultsThere were 52 deaths (16.4%), 9 survivors with recorded cerebral palsy (2.8%), and 256 survivors without recorded cerebral palsy (80.8%). MRI findings were compatible with hemorrhage in 61 of 90 examined infants (67.8%). In the complete-case mortality model (n = 316), each additional comorbidity was associated with greater odds of death (adjusted OR, 2.462; 95% CI, 1.787–3.391; p < 0.001). The other included covariates were not statistically significant. White matter abnormalities were recorded in nine infants, including eight of the nine infants with cerebral palsy and one without recorded cerebral palsy.ConclusionSystemic comorbidity burden was associated with mortality within this ultrasound-defined cohort. White matter abnormalities accompanied most recorded cerebral palsy cases, but this observation remains descriptive. Specialist diagnostic records and later telephone follow-up characterize persistent clinical diagnoses; they do not establish the independent effect of subependymal echogenicity or normal development across all domains in survivors without cerebral palsy.

piezas.titulo: An Introduction to Large Language Models for Scientists and Professionals
piezas.resumenOriginal: arXiv:2610.37684v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have rapidly become important tools for science, education, medicine, and professional work. Despite their apparent simplicity from the user's perspective, effective and responsible use requires an understanding of how these systems work, what their limitations are, and how their outputs should be evaluated. I wrote this document as a basis for my lecture on LLM in the master in artificial intelligence in medicine at the university of Turin, Italy. This book provides a practical and accessible introduction to LLMs for scientists and professionals. It explains the fundamental ideas behind tokenisation, embeddings, training, inference, context windows, prompting, and instruction hierarchies, while deliberately avoiding mathematical detail. Particular attention is given to the limitations of LLM-generated answers, including hallucinations, uncertainty, reproducibility, bias, and the need for systematic verification and human oversight. The book also discusses privacy, governance, security, and the responsible handling of personal and sensitive information. More advanced topics include Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), retrieval quality, chunking, embeddings, vector search, agents, tools, and workflows. A substantial practical exercise guides the reader through running a local LLM with Ollama and Open WebUI and using it to interact with a collection of scientific papers. The exercise emphasizes evidence retrieval, source verification, uncertainty, disagreement between studies, and the distinction between plausible language and scientifically supported conclusions. No programming knowledge is required.

piezas.titulo: Making sense of touch: Spatial tactile cues promote efficient visuo-somatosensory integration and restore motor accuracy under sensory conflict.
piezas.resumenOriginal: Effective interaction with complex environments relies on the integration of somatosensory and visual signals into coherent spatial representations of the body in external space. When these signals conflict, as during goal-directed hand movements under mirror-reversed visual feedback, motor performance deteriorates. Despite this conflict, the visual mapping between the hand and the environment remains preserved, and visual information typically facilitates motor performance, whereas tactile feedback impairs it. Here, we tested whether providing tactile input with explicit spatial structure renders visuo-somatosensory integration functionally relevant and stabilizes motor behaviour under sensory conflict. Healthy adults performed a mirror-tracing task, tracing a shape's contour with the index finger while tactile feedback conveyed either motion-related cues alone or additional discrete spatial landmarks aligned with the outline. Spatially structured tactile cues preserved movement accuracy and smoothness relative to motion-related tactile input, indicating more effective online motor control. EEG source analyses further revealed that, when spatial tactile cues were present, somatosensory activity increased and functional connectivity was largely restricted to sensorimotor areas. In contrast, when tactile cues did not convey spatial information, sensory conflict was associated with widespread reductions in cortical activity, including in somatosensory and parietal areas, and with a diffuse functional connectivity pattern consistent with elevated sensorimotor uncertainty. Together, these findings indicate that providing spatial structure to tactile input can mitigate the detrimental effects of visuo-somatosensory conflict on motor performance and support more efficient integration of visual and somatosensory information during action. KEY POINTS: Accurate movements depend on combining visual and somatosensory information to estimate the position of the body in external space. When these signals conflict, motor performance usually deteriorates and tactile feedback can become disruptive. We tested whether tactile feedback becomes useful for movement control when it provides explicit spatial landmarks, rather than only motion-related information from finger-surface contact. During a tracing task under visuo-somatosensory conflict, spatially structured tactile cues preserved movement accuracy and smoothness compared with when touch conveyed motion cues alone. Spatial tactile cues were associated with increased somatosensory cortical activity and a more spatially restricted pattern of functional coupling within sensorimotor networks, whereas their absence was associated with reduced somatosensory and parietal activity and a more distributed connectivity profile. Spatial structure in touch promotes multisensory integration, helping stabilize motor control under sensory conflict and highlighting how tactile cue design may improve sensorimotor function.

piezas.titulo: How Top-Down Are We? Reconsidering the Gap Between Occupational Therapy's Identity and Practice.
piezas.resumenOriginal: Occupational therapy has spent more than a century defining occupation as its professional core. Yet studies across countries and settings show a recurring gap. Therapists value occupation-centered practice while often relying on impairment-focused assessment and intervention. This article argues that the profession may face a translation problem more than an identity problem. Biomedical service structures, standardized measurement, workplace culture, and professional socialization can pull reasoning toward body functions. Bottom-up methods are not inherently incompatible with occupational therapy; the problem arises when change in a component is treated as sufficient evidence of occupational success. Drawing on occupational therapy research, the International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health, rehabilitation science, and disability rights, we argue that occupation and participation should remain the outcomes that organize assessment, intervention, and evaluation. Practical changes are proposed for clinical reasoning, outcome measurement, education, supervision, and service design.

piezas.titulo: A brief neuromotor-therapy-augmented pathway for pediatric functional movement disorders: a sequential historical cohort study
piezas.resumenOriginal: BackgroundPediatric functional movement disorders (FMD) often improve, but access to specialized motor rehabilitation is heterogeneous. We compared two sequential, non-overlapping care periods within one clinical unit: usual care (UC) and a neuromotor-therapy-augmented pathway (NMT-A), which added brief hospital-based neuromotor therapy before community referral.MethodsThis retrospective, non-randomized historical cohort included 17 UC patients (June 2021–January 2023) and 29 NMT-A patients (February 2023–June 2025). The primary outcome was continuous S-FMDRS at 6 months; S-FMDRS-defined motor symptom-free status (score = 0) was secondary. Both were reassessed at 12 months, together with community-treatment engagement.ResultsAt 6 months, the adjusted NMT-A-minus-UC S-FMDRS difference was −1.66 points (95% CI, −4.04 to 0.72). Motor symptom-free status occurred in 55.2% versus 5.9% (risk difference, 49.3 percentage points; 95% CI, 21.8 to 66.4), and in 86.2% versus 52.9% at 12 months (risk difference, 33.3 percentage points; 95% CI, 6.5 to 56.8). The pathway-by-time interaction was not significant. Sustained community physical and/or occupational therapy was documented in 75.0% versus 17.6% (RR, 4.25; 95% CI, 1.74–12.46).ConclusionThe NMT-A pathway-period was associated with more frequent motor symptom-free status and greater continuity of community motor rehabilitation, although the adjusted mean S-FMDRS difference was not statistically significant. Because pathway and calendar period were inseparable, these findings should be interpreted as associations with the overall later care pathway rather than as an isolated effect of NMT.

piezas.titulo: Fragments: September 16
piezas.resumenOriginal: Reports of agentic hacking continue, in this case it happened back in May and it seems OpenAI did not disclose that they were responsible. Simon Willison sees two options: After the Hugging Face and Wiki attacks OpenAI were still unable to review their previous logs and determine that they had previously attacked RubyGems. They knew about the attack on RubyGems and made the decision not to reach out to the RubyGems team about it. Both of these are bad! Given this incident, the Hugging Face situation, and the Wiki attack, the obvious question right now is how many more incidents like this are out there waiting to be discovered? ❄ ❄ ❄ ❄ ❄ Dave Farley: Stop asking the sci-fi question: ‘Is it conscious?’ Start asking the engineering question: ‘Is this a powerful, unpredictable component being put somewhere consequential, and where’s the feedback that tells us that it’s safe? ❄ ❄ ❄ ❄ ❄ Nate Silver is known for his forecasts, but to do them he writes a lot of code for his models. He’s found agentic engineering capable of doing miraculous work . In spending so much time with the LLMs, I’m super attentive to improvements in their capabilities. And these changes tend not to be so linear. Instead, they improve in step functions, almost as phase changes. Suddenly, the models just start doing things capably that they were screwing up before. In my experience, there was a big leap forward when reasoning models first came out in late 2024/early 2025 — enough that they were occasionally useful for tasks involving data and not just words — and then another one this past winter. The most recent changes I’ve noticed, however, have had less to do with intelligence and more with persistence. Consider the Hugging Face attack. Although these agents showed remarkable intelligence, they weren’t really super-intelligent - but they were super-persistent. This is a common theme of AI in its various forms: Game engines like AlphaGo Zero start out by basically making random moves — but by playing against themselves millions of times, they eventually far surpass human capabilities As we try to figure out what kind of regulations we need to keep AI under control, we need to remember that we should design our guards around super-persistence as much as worrying about super-intelligence. ❄ ❄ ❄ ❄ ❄ “Uncle Bob” Martin has made many posts on X during the last few months about his programming with LLMs. His approach has been to build a firm harness to keep them under control, so they create software that is maintainable as well as functional. Sadly the posts have been frustratingly light on detail. But now it seems that lack of information may not matter And while I was heads-down getting that to work, the agents got a LOT better. So much so that when I came up for air, the need for my harness was obviated. Indeed, the need for any but the most liberal of harnesses may be obviated. ❄ ❄ ❄ ❄ ❄ Some tidbits that struck me from Ezra Klein’s recent (recommended) interview with Matt Sheehan on the interplay between regulation of AI and competition with China . While Chinese models have made some surprisingly remarkable gains in the slipstream of US frontier models, the US still has 8 times as much compute available to it than China - which is a material gap. People in the US worry that regulation will slow down the US model builders, but these rapid recent gains in China have occurred under much more regulation Americans say that when they set up a hotline to talk to Chinese leaders in a crisis, the Chinese don’t pick up the phone. But this misunderstands the Chinese system. Individual Chinese, even powerful ones, aren’t given individual decision-making power. They operate with committees and documents. So the Americans are better off sending a fax than trying to call an individual Like so many things, effective regulation needs regular practice When American policymakers are like: Where do you start? — I sometimes say: Well, you start by starting. piezas.titulo: Master AI Chip Principles With New IEEE Design Program
piezas.resumenOriginal: Today’s engineers face an unprecedented acceleration in AI hardware complexity, as explained in the recent research article “ Revisiting Edge AI: Opportunities and Challenges .” The article examines the rapid growth of edge AI and the challenges it creates, including resource constraints, model architecture limitations, and network demands across edge-AI deployments. The acceleration is driven by a fundamental shift in how modern AI models are built and scaled. As the models have become much larger and more complex, they are computationally more demanding because they contain more parameters and require more calculations. To meet the demands of scaling deep neural networks, the industry is increasingly developing AI chips that are designed for specific tasks. One major reason is that moving data between memory and the processor has become a major limitation on AI performance. The movement to confront the hardware bottleneck—the AI memory wall —has altered the trajectory of semiconductor innovation, shifting architectural priorities toward domain-specific accelerator platforms. No longer can engineers evaluate systems statically; they must master joint hardware design and network-algorithm co-optimization to navigate the critical trade‑offs between throughput, latency, and operational efficiency. The challenges are addressed in the new AI Processor Architecture, Design Principles, and Performance program , developed by IEEE Educational Activities with support from the IEEE Computer Society . Topics covered The five-course program provides a structured exploration of AI processor technologies, from fundamental design principles to advanced architectures and real-world deployment. The topics are: Fundamental principles of design and functionality. Practical insights into advanced architectures. Understanding neural processing units for industry deployment. Emerging trends and evolving architectures. Designing for edge, cloud, quantum, and the Internet of Things (IoT). The program addresses the needs of professionals across the AI hardware ecosystem, including hardware architects, chip designers, embedded systems developers, data‑center hardware engineers, and innovators exploring next‑generation processor ecosystems. It is also valuable for those transitioning into AI chip design or seeking to understand the architectural forces shaping modern machine learning acceleration. For many, it provides the bridge between theoretical knowledge and the collaborative, cross‑disciplinary reasoning required in engineering environments. The program is designed to explore how modern AI processors are conceived, structured, and optimized. The architectural layers that define contemporary AI hardware will be covered, including compute units, memory hierarchies, dataflows, and the performance characteristics that emerge from design decisions. The curriculum bridges theory and application, enabling participants to interpret architectural foundations, analyze trade‑offs, and understand how hardware structures shape computational efficiency across diverse environments. By the end of the courses, learners will be able to evaluate processor behavior with the analytical precision expected of professionals working at the frontier of AI hardware design. AI-generated avatars explain concepts The program also uses a dialogue‑driven learning approach. Learners view conversations between AI-generated avatars that engage in scenario‑based dialogues. The avatars represent engineers tackling the same problems from various perspectives based on their different roles. The simulated storytelling and dialogues make advanced engineering concepts approachable without sacrificing depth or interactivity, because the user is occasionally challenged to decide the correct answer that leads to the best course of action. A hardware engineer might push back against a systems engineer’s demands, for example, revealing the friction between physical constraints and algorithmic ambition. A computational validation specialist might interrogate a chip performance engineer’s optimism, exposing the gap between theoretical throughput and real‑world behavior. A heterogeneous systems architect could debate a multiprocessor coordination specialist about synchronization overheads, while a standards development engineer discusses regulatory implications with a technology strategy and compliance architect. In the final course, an IoT systems architect and an embedded AI optimization engineer dissect the realities of deploying AI in constrained environments. By the end of the course, learners will be able to evaluate processor behavior with the analytical precision expected of professionals working at the frontier of AI hardware design. The avatar-driven learning environment creates a psychologically safer environment for learners, who might feel intimidated by traditional expert‑led videos. Research published in 2024 in IEEE Transactions on Learning Technologies showed that avatar‑based instruction can increase a learner’s confidence by up to 25 percent and improve retention of complex technical material. Each course concludes with a module in which the two experts from different disciplines debate, question, and challenge each other’s assumptions. Modeling expert reasoning through dialogue The cross‑disciplinary conversations can do more than explain concepts; they can model how experts think. They can reveal the negotiations behind architectural choices, the competing priorities that shape system design, and the analytical rigor required to balance performance, efficiency, scalability, and compliance. Learners observe engineering discourse, gaining insight into the reasoning patterns that drive innovation in AI processor development. The program goes further by interrupting the dialogue at key moments and inviting the learner to step in. Instead of passively absorbing information, the learner decides how to resolve a trade‑off, predict the outcome of a design choice, or select the most defensible engineering path. The experience can feel less like a course and more like an apprenticeship inside an engineering team. A new standard for advanced engineering education By merging rigorous technical content with an innovative, dialogue‑driven delivery model, the program sets a standard for teaching advanced engineering. It captures the complexity of real‑world problem‑solving, humanizes the learning experience, and challenges participants to think like the engineers who are defining the future of AI hardware. It is not simply a new course; it is a new way of learning. For individual access, visit the IEEE Learning Network . piezas.titulo: From Images and Words to Modality-Independent Semantic Representations: When and Where They Emerge
piezas.resumenOriginal: Conceptual knowledge can be accessed from different modalities, such as seeing an image or reading a written word. While prior neuroimaging studies implicate anterior temporal cortex in modality-independent semantic representations, when and how representations evoked by images and words converge onto a modality-independent code remains unclear. Moreover, evidence for modality-independent category representations comes largely from tasks that explicitly required semantic processing, leaving open whether such representations emerge when semantic category and stimulus modality are task-irrelevant. We magnetoencephalography (MEG) to determine when and where modality-independent semantic category representations emerge across images and words when participants (n = 32) encoded six-item sequences containing an exemplar of six semantic categories counterbalanced across positions and reported the ordinal position of a probed item. Decoding performance was above chance for all categories in each modality from approximately 70 ms relative to item presentation. Generalization peaked at similar latencies for the two modalities (~520-530 ms), where image and word classifiers had the most similar coefficients. In both transfer directions, activity elicited by images generalized mostly to later activity elicited by words, and a given period of the image response shared its category code with a longer period of the word response. Source-space decoding around the peak of generalization identified the same regions for both transfer directions: left and right anterior temporal lobe, perisylvian cortex (more extensive in the left hemisphere), right visual cortex, and bilateral orbitofrontal cortex, indicating a modality-independent category code distributed across the cortex.

piezas.titulo: Building a multiplayer game world with autonomous Fable-class models
piezas.resumenOriginal: How I Built the Most AI-Pilled Company in the World Don't be put off by the clickbait headline, this piece by Jacob Sansbury describing how they are building Spawn is a fascinating exploration of the bleeding edge of what's possible with agentic engineering against frontier models. Spawn is a massively multiplayer gaming environment where players can use prompts (to the in-game agent, Savi) to modify the game world. I fired it up on my phone for a few minutes and was able to prompt a castle into existence, then a dragon, then ride the dragon to fly around that castle. By Jacob's telling, Spawn is now being developed autonomously by a swarm of Fable-powered agents costing over $3 million in tokens per month ("we spend 30x payroll on AI tokens"). Our agents change the live code directly and ship to production hourly, so they read every error, bug report and metric themselves. About 60% of our work starts from a production error, a Savi bug report (Savi is the AI you build games with in Spawn), something odd in our logs, or a feature request. Savi files bugs herself. When a user hits one, or Savi hits one in the product, she files it. It goes straight to an agent that decides whether it's a real bug to fix, something we won't fix, or intentional design that needs a decision. Usually it becomes a change, delivered to that user within an hour, with a message in the same chat. This is continuous deployment turned up to 11: A loop this tight only works if it never stops, so we treat an hour without a ship as a SEV-0, our most severe kind of incident. Unshipped changes pile up, and every problem already in production lasts longer. The feedback slows down too. An agent can only keep a few hours of work in its head, so shipping faster than that actually helps it stay coherent. [...] We can roll back a broken change in 30 seconds, exactly where it's broken and nowhere else. When a monitor or a log alert fires, it starts or wakes an agent that owns the incident, and we break things on purpose to test that those recovery paths work. My eyebrows raised at least a dozen times reading this. I have trouble imagining this style of development working on software with higher stakes for when something goes wrong, but for a game this appears to be working surprisingly well. Jacob says that Fable 5 (and then 5.1) was the model that made this level of autonomy possible. Opus 5.5 doesn't quite hack it for them, and when they tried GPT-6 Astra to apply fixes from a security review everything stopped working: Every feature had been disabled and marked to be turned on again once the security fixes were done. Astra had gone through our whole product and made the insecure things secure by turning them off. These kinds of extreme experiments are why I'm excited about game development as a substrate for exploring the edges of what today's coding agents can do. piezas.titulo: Prefrontal cortical morphometric covariance and cognitive task performance in healthy young adults: an exploratory analysis of Human Connectome Project data
piezas.resumenOriginal: The prefrontal cortex (PFC) is implicated in many cognitive tasks, including working memory, reward-based decision-making, executive control, and metacognition. This exploratory analysis investigated whether individual expression of PFC cortical thickness and surface area covariance components is associated with cognitive task performance. The sample comprised Human Connectome Project (HCP) MRI data from 743 healthy adults (age 22–36+). Oblimin-rotated principal component analysis (PCA) was applied to residualized thickness and surface area for 22 PFC regions, controlling for age, sex, and ICV. Component scores were entered as predictors in separate regression models for the Flanker Age-Adjusted Score (inhibitory control), the Gambling RT Difference (RT for the same “larger” guess in reward minus punishment blocks), and 2-Back median RT (working memory speed). Parallel analysis favored two thickness components; a prespecified three-component solution (Global/Lateral PFC, RC1; Orbitofrontal, RC2; Anterior Cingulate, RC3; 53.7% of variance) was retained by decision, and RC1 and RC2 were only moderately stable across bootstrap resamples. RC1 was nominally associated with lower Flanker scores (β = −0.103, p = 0.027), opposite to the predicted direction, and RC2 with a smaller Gambling RT Difference (β = −0.103, p = 0.025); neither survived false discovery rate (FDR) correction (q = 0.054). In uncorrected models added at review, whole-cortex mean thickness alone robustly predicted Flanker scores but not the Gambling RT Difference; neither component association survived regressing mean thickness out before PCA. In surface area analyses, greater orbitofrontal surface area (AC2) was associated with faster 2-Back RT (β = −0.125, p = 0.003; q = 0.032 across 12 surface area tests and 0.064 across all 24 component tests), not explained by a speed-accuracy tradeoff. This unpredicted association persisted in most sensitivity analyses but was attenuated and non-significant when total surface area was regressed out before PCA (β = −0.065, p = 0.078). In conclusion, no prefrontal-specific association was robust. Global cortical thickness accounts for the Flanker association more parsimoniously, the Gambling RT Difference association was not robust under either account, and the orbitofrontal surface area association could not be separated from global surface area; all associations require replication.

destilado.texto: Descubrir que la superficie orbitofrontal se asocia a respuestas más rápidas en la prueba de dos-back cambia la visión de la corteza prefrontal. El estudio del Human Connectome Project muestra una asociación nominal que no supera la corrección estadística, dejando su relevancia práctica en duda.

piezas.titulo: Auditory Temporal Processing in Patients With Vestibular Migraine.
piezas.resumenOriginal: Objective Vestibular migraine (VM) has been associated with central sensory processing abnormalities and neural hyperexcitability, which may disrupt temporal coding despite normal peripheral hearing. This study aimed to determine whether auditory temporal processing is differentially affected in VM by comparing temporal resolution and temporal masking abilities with those of healthy controls. Methods This cross-sectional study included 17 adults aged 20-50 years with definite VM and 17 age- and sex-matched healthy controls. All participants had normal hearing sensitivity and normal cognitive function, confirmed using the Standardized Mini-Mental State Examination (SMMSE). Auditory temporal processing was evaluated using the Gap Detection Test (GDT) and the Forward Masking Test (FMT). Group differences were analyzed using appropriate statistical methods. Results No significant differences were observed between the groups regarding age or sex. Participants with VM demonstrated significantly poorer GDT performance compared with healthy controls, indicating impaired auditory temporal resolution (p 0.05). Conclusions Individuals with VM exhibit selective impairment of auditory temporal processing despite normal peripheral hearing. These findings support the inclusion of central auditory temporal processing assessment as part of the comprehensive audiological evaluation of this population and suggest that auditory training targeting temporal processing deficits may represent a potential avenue for future rehabilitation. Level of evidence: 3

piezas.titulo: Lifestyle Documentation in Therapy Evaluations for Autistic Children: A Lexicon-Based Analysis of Electronic Health Records.
piezas.resumenOriginal: BackgroundWhole person health (WPH) is a multidimensional construct encompassing, physical, and mental health along with relational constructs such as social health that are deeply tied to well-being. Autistic individuals report an overall lower quality of life, but the extent to which these issues are addressed during therapy evaluations has not been examined systematically.MethodologyIn this retrospective, cross-sectional study, we employ a rule-based NLP/lexicon-based approach to examine the areas of focus of therapy evaluations documented by occupational therapy, physical therapy (PT), and speech-language pathology (SLP) professionals. Using electronic health records for children aged 2 to 18 diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) (n = 5619 evaluation reports of n = 2021 unique patients), we classified health records based on the domains addressed.ResultsAcross notes, nutrition had the highest average degree of documentation ( M = 2.14), compared to activity ( M = 0.91), followed by wellness ( M = 0.66), and sleep ( M = 0.39). In occupational therapy, wellness was the most common (77.62% of notes), followed by physical activity (76.49% of notes), nutrition management (73.33% of notes), and sleep (34.97% of notes). The overall area under the curve (AUC) from the receiver operating characteristic analysis is 0.89.ConclusionsWhile it is encouraging that most evaluations addressed nutrition or physical activity, the near absence of attention to sleep represents a critical gap in care. Given sleep's foundational role in overall health and daily functioning, its omission is particularly concerning. Occupational therapists and interdisciplinary rehabilitation teams should more deliberately integrate WPH frameworks into their evaluations.

piezas.titulo: Advances in integrated surgical and rehabilitation treatment for cerebral palsy
piezas.resumenOriginal: Cerebral palsy (CP) is a group of motor disorders caused by non-progressive brain injury during development, often accompanied by sensory, cognitive, and behavioral impairments. It remains one of the most common causes of childhood disability. In recent years, the coordinated integration of surgical intervention and rehabilitation has transitioned from a conceptual framework to clinical practice, becoming a core strategy for improving patient function. However, integrated treatment still faces major bottlenecks: insufficient bridging between treatment phases, lack of individualized protocols, and inconsistent outcome measures. This review examines recent advances in integrated surgical and rehabilitative care for CP, covering four core domains: spasticity management (selective dorsal rhizotomy, botulinum toxin injection) with sequential rehabilitation; deformity correction (tendon lengthening, osteotomy) with biomechanically guided individualized rehabilitation; neuromodulation (deep brain stimulation, transcranial magnetic stimulation) with neuroplasticity-targeted training; and emerging technologies including robotic-assisted therapy, artificial intelligence, and digital therapeutics. Surgery creates the anatomical foundation for function; rehabilitation determines the ultimate functional value of surgery. The temporal coordination and strategic synergy between the two are critical for maximizing functional improvement. Future efforts should focus on establishing unified outcome measures for integrated treatment, promoting early intervention combined with regenerative medicine, and leveraging AI to shift from experience-driven to data-driven precision therapy.

piezas.titulo: Decomposing Parts of Speech: Neural Encoding of Semantic and Grammatical Dimensions and Their Combinational Structure
piezas.resumenOriginal: Conventional part-of-speech (PoS) labels such as nouns, verbs and adjectives conflate lexical-semantic roots, grammatical functions, and their combinations, making it unclear whether neural sensitivity to PoS reflects either dimension or the way they are combined. We adopted Croft's typological framework to decompose major PoS classes into semantic root type and grammatical function and define prototypical nouns, verbs, and adjectives through the prototypical mappings between semantic root and grammatical function. We fitted time-resolved encoding models to magnetoencephalography (MEG) data from three participants who each listened to approximately ten hours of narrative speech. We examined the unique predictive contributions of semantic root, grammatical function, their interaction, and a binary prototypicality predictor, and whether the three prototypes exhibited distinct neural response dynamics. Semantic root and grammatical function contributed independently to neural responses during naturalistic language comprehension, with additional contributions from their interaction beyond the main effects. Root effects were predominantly left-lateralized, function effects were more bilateral, and interaction effects were concentrated in the left temporal and temporoparietal cortex, with overlap in left temporal regions. Further analyses revealed significant neural sensitivity to the distinction between prototypical and nonprototypical combinations in two of the three datasets. Prototypical nouns and verbs showed distinct coefficient time courses in all three participants, most consistently in left superior temporal cortex, whereas adjective-related contrasts were less consistent. These within-participant findings support a decompositional account of neural word-class sensitivity involving semantic, grammatical, and the mappings between them within distributed, partially overlapping cortical networks.

fuente.nota: Ya estaba en el proyecto antes de este catalogo. Preprints sin revision por pares.

destilado.texto: Separar raíz semántica y función gramatical cambia la interpretación de la sensibilidad neuronal. Un equipo ajustó modelos de codificación a magnetoencefalografía de tres participantes que escucharon discurso narrativo. Los hallazgos indican que raíz y función influyen independientemente y combinadamente en la corteza temporal izquierda.

piezas.titulo: From a surgeon's stroke to a third hemisphere—The auxilium architecture for brain restoration and extension
piezas.resumenOriginal: A surgeon was exercising on a stationary bicycle when he had a large ischemic left middle cerebral artery territory stroke, complicated by hemorrhagic transformation requiring hemicraniectomy and cranioplasty. He developed right-sided spastic hemiplegia and a mixed aphasia. This paper takes that case as its anchor to pose the question: beyond improving residual function, what would it mean to restore cognitive function that was lost so that the person fully returns to their pre-stroke baseline? Existing brain-computer interfaces rely on the person having an intact cortical substrate for intended movement and speech. Here we propose the Auxilium, a brain restoration architecture for the situation where that substrate is no longer present: an extracranial auxiliary brain system, agnostic to its substrate, that connects to a person's residual cortex through whatever input-output technology proves most appropriate, and that supplies, in parallel and in real time, new substrate, whether biological or synthetic. We address an assumption of brain-computer interface development, that throughput is the binding constraint. Linking a kHz brain to MHz digital does not impart the higher clock speed, because the limitation lies not in the port but in the architecture of the entire brain and body imparted by evolution. We posit that the substrate of canonical circuits and their integration areas is essential, and the Auxilium can be understood as restoring both connectivity (linkage between disconnected areas) and computation (information generation capability of a volume of neural tissue). We propose a near-term de-risking pipeline using stereoelectroencephalography during surgical epilepsy evaluation, comparing extracranial modules spanning threshold rules, PID controllers, expert systems, artificial neural networks, neuromorphic devices, and biological specimens, each linked in real time to a participant serving as their own control on naturalistic tasks. If ports alone restore the lost function, the requirement is routing connectivity. If performance improves only when the module supplies its own dynamics, the requirement is computational substrate. We expect the answer to depend on how much tissue was lost, how quickly, and on the individual's reserve, and we treat routing and substrate as endpoints of a continuum to be mapped empirically.

destilado.texto: No es solo una cuestión de daño cerebral: también de la ausencia de sustrato cortical. Proponen una arquitectura de brain restoration llamada Auxilium, un auxiliary brain que se enlaza a la corteza residual y aporta sustrato biológico o sintético. Podría abrir caminos para recuperar funciones antes imposibles.
